data.name: February
data.gender_notes: February is used as a neutral name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'februare', meaning 'to purify'. February is the second month of the Gregorian calendar and is associated with purification and renewal. In the Roman calendar, it was the first month and was dedicated to the Roman god Februus, who was believed to purify the Roman army. The name February carries the meaning “Month of purification” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose February usually hope their child will grow to embody month of purification and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: February symbolizes purification, new beginnings, and renewal. It is a time to let go of old habits and to embrace new growth and transformation.
data.etymology: February belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Month of purification.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of February total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: February is also the month that honors St. Brigid of Ireland, who is the patron saint of poets, dairymaids, farmers, and healers. Her feast day is celebrated on February 1st with various traditional Irish practices, such as making "Brigid's crosses" from rushes or reeds to ward off evil and bring blessings of health, fertility, and livestock prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian theology, February is a reminder to purify our hearts, minds, and souls in preparation for the upcoming Lenten season. It is a time for introspection, contemplation, and spiritual growth as we reflect on our relationships with God, self, and others. The purification rituals of ancient civilizations have morphed into the contemporary practice of confession and penance in the Christian faith. By embracing the spiritual opportunities of February, we can draw closer to God and live more fully in His love.
